reconfigure.title: Update the connection details
reconfigure.description: Device ID `{device_id}` is fixed: it is what identifies this entry, so a different device ID would be a different device. The other three do move. Re-pairing in the Smart Life app mints a new local key, a DHCP lease can move the IP address, and a firmware update can move the protocol version. The new values are tried against the device before anything is saved — if they fail, the entry is left exactly as it was.

user.title: Connect to the diffuser
user.description: IP address, device ID and local key come from `tuya-local-key`, which logs in by QR code and needs no Tuya IoT developer account; the protocol version is `3.5` on this unit. The README's **Set it up** section has the steps. The local key is a live credential — it is stored in Home Assistant's config entry like any other integration secret.

error.cannot_connect: The device did not answer with these credentials. Check the IP address, local key and protocol version.

init.title: Polling
init.description: How often to read the device. Lower is fresher but competes with the Tuya app, which may share the device's single local connection.

device_unreachable.title: The diffuser at {host} has stopped answering
device_unreachable.description:
No poll has succeeded for over {minutes} minutes — {failures} consecutive attempts. Two different things produce exactly this, and Home Assistant cannot tell them apart from here:

1. **The diffuser is off, asleep, or off the network.** Check that it has power, and that `{host}` is still its address — a DHCP lease can move it.
2. **It was re-paired in the Smart Life app.** Re-pairing mints a new local key and the old one stops decrypting immediately. The device ID survives; the key does not.

If it is powered on and on the network, the second one is the answer: **Settings → Devices & Services → Arozen EON Pro 2 → ⋮ → Reconfigure**. The new IP address, local key and protocol version are tried against the device before anything is saved, so a wrong value leaves the entry exactly as it was. The entry keeps its identity, which is why this is not "delete it and add it again" — your automations and entity IDs survive.

This card clears itself the moment one poll succeeds.
